input.question: If I brush my teeth twice everyday, why are they never fully white? Is there a way to get them there?
input.ground_truth: Natural, healthy teeth are not white, they are ivory colored. The desire for white teeth is an artificial standard pushed by the beauty industry, hence all the products that will whiten your teeth... for a fee.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If I brush my teeth twice everyday, why are they never fully white? Is there a way to get them there?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your teeth are like a piece of paper. When you eat or drink things like chocolate, tea, or soda, it’s like drawing with a marker on the paper. Brushing your teeth is like wiping the paper with a cloth, but sometimes the marker doesn’t come all the way off, so the paper stays a little colored.

Even if you brush really well every day, some of the coloring stays stuck in tiny spots on your teeth that are really hard to clean. That’s why your teeth might look a little yellow or not super, super white.

But don’t worry! There are special toothpastes and things your grown-up can use that can help make your teeth a little whiter. Also, if you keep brushing and flossing, your teeth will be as clean and white as they can be for you! But everyone’s teeth are a little different, so they might not be as white as the paper was when it was brand new. That’s totally normal! 😊
